correctness.rationale: The S_n action permutes off-diagonal edges transitively and preserves both edge subspaces. Any equivariant vertex-potential-to-cycle map has the form a x_i+b x_j+c sum_k x_k and zero row/column sums force a=b=c=0 for all n>=3; hence there are no intertwiners cut-to-cycle nor cycle-to-cut. Group averaging forces each canonical orthogonal projector to be the unique equivariant projection and norm-minimal for all invariant norms. An explicit Laplacian solution for injection along an edge determines five disjoint current orbits, their signs and counts; their absolute sum is ||Q||_1=(3n-4)/n. Diagonal resistance (2n-1)/(n(n-1)) gives ||C||_1=2(2n²-6n+3)/(n(n-1)), with symmetric matrices equating l1 and l-infinity norms and a direct polynomial sign giving crossover n=5. Independent exact rational Laplacian inversion verified every column through n=8, including boundary n=3. The all-n proof rests on representation and electrical identities, not the finite range.

value.rationale: The result determines relative projection constants of natural cut and cycle Banach subspaces for an infinite edge-transitive graph family, identifies the unique equivariant minimizers and a sharp crossover in norm dominance. It extends a previously known n=4 cube special case to a family-wide structural calculation.

limitations: Relative projection constants in fixed edge ambient space, not absolute projection constants.
Equivariant uniqueness only, not uniqueness among all norm-minimizing projections.
General invariant-norm optimality does not give numerical formula for arbitrary invariant norms.
Ye–Yan 2019 original article full text was inaccessible; it could contain stronger transfer-current formulas than indicated by title.
